title: Grenada Achieves Independence from the United Kingdom
description: On February 7, 1974, Grenada became an independent state within the Commonwealth, ending British colonial rule under a Westminster-style constitution. Independence took place against a backdrop of strikes and unrest opposing Premier Eric Gairy, with Queen Elizabeth II remaining head of state and Gairy assuming office as the country's first prime minister.

title: Eric Gairy Becomes First Prime Minister
description: Eric Matthew Gairy, the dominant figure of Grenadian politics since the 1950s and leader of the Grenada United Labour Party (GULP), assumed office as the country's first prime minister at independence. His increasingly authoritarian rule, reliance on the paramilitary Mongoose Gang, and eccentric foreign policy preoccupations would define the post-independence period.

title: Grenada Joins the United Nations
description: On September 17, 1974, Grenada was admitted to the United Nations as the 138th member state, formalizing its international personality as the smallest independent country in the Western Hemisphere. UN membership offered a platform for small island state diplomacy on decolonization, climate, and development issues.

title: Founding Membership of CARICOM Anchors Regional Integration
description: Grenada was a founding signatory of the Treaty of Chaguaramas establishing the Caribbean Community (CARICOM) in 1973 and entered the bloc as a sovereign state in 1974. Membership tied trade, foreign policy and functional cooperation to the wider English-speaking Caribbean and provided diplomatic cover for a small new state.

title: New Jewel Movement Seizes Power in Bloodless Coup
description: On March 13, 1979, while Eric Gairy was overseas, the New Jewel Movement under Maurice Bishop launched an armed takeover of the True Blue army barracks and the Radio Grenada station, seizing the country in a near-bloodless coup. Bishop suspended the 1974 constitution and proclaimed the People's Revolutionary Government, the first and only successful armed leftist takeover in the English-speaking Caribbean.

title: People's Revolutionary Government Suspends Constitution
description: After the March 1979 coup, the People's Revolutionary Government (PRG) ruled by decree under People's Laws, suspending the 1974 independence constitution and indefinitely postponing elections. The PRG combined social spending on health and literacy with detention of opponents, censorship of independent media and a one-party state structure dominated by the New Jewel Movement.

title: Cuba and Soviet Bloc Open Aid Relationship with Grenada
description: Within weeks of the March 1979 coup, Cuba dispatched advisors, doctors and military personnel to Grenada and Bishop established close ties with Havana, Moscow and other Eastern bloc capitals. Cuban and Soviet aid funded a new international airport at Point Salines and ideological training, dramatically expanding Cold War tensions in the eastern Caribbean.

title: Carter Administration Imposes Diplomatic and Aid Squeeze
description: Washington responded to the New Jewel Movement takeover by withholding aid, blocking multilateral lending and warning regional governments against military cooperation with the PRG. The escalating diplomatic squeeze pushed Bishop further into the Cuban-Soviet orbit and set the stage for direct US military action four years later.

title: Construction of Point Salines International Airport with Cuban Labour
description: The PRG broke ground on a 9,000-foot runway at Point Salines built primarily with Cuban construction workers and engineers, financed by a coalition including Cuba, Libya, Algeria and the European Community. Washington characterized the project as a Soviet-Cuban military airfield, while the PRG presented it as essential tourism infrastructure for jet-capable arrivals.

title: Detention of Trade Unionists and Press Closure
description: The PRG closed the independent Torchlight newspaper, refused to license alternative outlets and detained an estimated several hundred political opponents without trial under People's Law 8. Internal critics including former allies were held at Richmond Hill Prison, foreshadowing the leadership rupture of 1983.

title: PRG Adopts Centrally Planned National Development Plan
description: The People's Revolutionary Government published a national development plan emphasizing state-led industrialization, expansion of cooperatives and an enlarged public sector role in nutmeg, cocoa and tourism. The plan combined Cuban-style social investment with conventional Caribbean export sectors, partly funded by concessional loans from socialist bloc partners.

title: Leadership Split Between Bishop and Coard Faction
description: Through 1983 a power struggle deepened inside the New Jewel Movement central committee between Prime Minister Maurice Bishop and Deputy Prime Minister Bernard Coard's hardline faction over joint leadership and Leninist party discipline. The dispute moved from internal debate to open confrontation by October as the army leadership aligned with Coard.

title: Bishop Overthrown and Executed at Fort Rupert
description: On October 19, 1983, soldiers loyal to the Coard faction stormed Fort Rupert (Fort George) and executed Maurice Bishop along with cabinet ministers Unison Whiteman, Jacqueline Creft, Norris Bain and Fitzroy Bain after a crowd had freed Bishop from house arrest. A Revolutionary Military Council under General Hudson Austin took power and imposed a four-day shoot-on-sight curfew.

title: United States Operation Urgent Fury Invades Grenada
description: On October 25, 1983, around 7,300 US military personnel together with troops from Jamaica, Barbados and other OECS states landed in Grenada under Operation Urgent Fury, citing the safety of US medical students and a request from the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States. The Reagan administration's invasion overthrew the Revolutionary Military Council within days against limited Grenadian and Cuban resistance.

title: Interim Advisory Council Restores Constitutional Order
description: Following the US-led intervention, Governor-General Sir Paul Scoon invoked reserve powers to appoint an interim Advisory Council under Nicholas Brathwaite to administer the country. The council restored the suspended 1974 constitution, prepared the ground for elections and accepted continued US military and police assistance to stabilize the island.

title: New National Party Wins First Post-Invasion Election
description: On December 3, 1984, the New National Party led by Herbert Blaize won 14 of 15 seats in the first general election since 1976, defeating Eric Gairy's GULP and the rump Maurice Bishop Patriotic Movement. The vote re-established competitive parliamentary politics under the restored constitution and confirmed a centre-right pro-Western foreign policy realignment.

title: Trial of the Grenada 17 for Bishop Killings
description: Bernard Coard, his wife Phyllis Coard, General Hudson Austin and fourteen others were tried before a Grenadian court on charges arising from the October 1983 killings, with fourteen initially sentenced to death in December 1986. The proceedings, conducted under restored constitutional law, became a long-running symbol of post-revolutionary accountability and contested justice.

title: Brathwaite NDC Government Takes Office
description: The March 1990 general election produced no overall majority, and Nicholas Brathwaite's National Democratic Congress formed a minority government with the support of independent legislators. The Brathwaite administration pursued cautious economic adjustment, infrastructure rehabilitation after Hurricane Hugo damage and rebuilding of administrative capacity.

title: Death Sentences for Grenada 17 Commuted to Life Imprisonment
description: In August 1991 the death sentences imposed on Bernard Coard and the other Grenada 17 defendants were commuted to life imprisonment, ending a long appeal saga over the death penalty. The decision became a reference point for Caribbean debate over capital punishment and the unresolved political legacy of October 1983.

title: Keith Mitchell and the New National Party Win Power
description: On June 20, 1995, Keith Mitchell led the New National Party to victory in the general election, ending the NDC's term and beginning what would become three consecutive Mitchell governments. Mitchell campaigned on economic liberalization, tourism expansion and improved relations with Washington and Taiwan.

title: Grenada Switches Recognition from Beijing to Taipei
description: In 1997 the Mitchell government switched diplomatic recognition from the People's Republic of China to the Republic of China (Taiwan), securing aid packages, scholarships and infrastructure financing. The decision drew Beijing's protest and was reversed in 2005 when Grenada re-established ties with the PRC after Hurricane Ivan reconstruction needs grew.

title: NNP Sweeps All 15 Parliamentary Seats
description: The January 18, 1999 general election delivered an unprecedented 15-0 sweep of the House of Representatives to Keith Mitchell's New National Party, the first single-party clean sweep in Grenada's electoral history. The result entrenched Mitchell's dominance but raised concerns about absent parliamentary opposition and concentration of executive power.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission on Revolution Era
description: Prime Minister Keith Mitchell appointed a Truth and Reconciliation Commission in 2001 (work commenced from 2000 preparations) chaired by Reverend Donald Chambers to investigate human rights abuses during the Gairy years, the People's Revolutionary Government and the 1983 invasion. Its 2006 report documented detentions, killings and the unresolved location of Maurice Bishop's remains.

title: Mitchell NNP Wins Third Consecutive Term
description: On November 27, 2003, Keith Mitchell's NNP narrowly won a third consecutive general election with eight seats to the NDC's seven, on a platform stressing tourism investment and offshore financial services. The slim majority signalled rising voter frustration with corruption allegations swirling around the long-running Mitchell government.

title: Hurricane Ivan Devastates 89% of Housing Stock
description: On September 7, 2004, Hurricane Ivan struck Grenada as a Category 3 storm directly across the island, killing dozens of people and damaging or destroying around 89% of all housing units. The hurricane wrecked the nutmeg industry, knocked out essential infrastructure and inflicted damage estimated at roughly twice annual GDP, the worst natural disaster in modern Grenadian history.

title: Hurricane Emily Strikes Recovering Island
description: On July 14, 2005, Hurricane Emily passed close to Grenada as a Category 1 hurricane, killing one person and inflicting fresh damage on housing and agriculture barely ten months after Hurricane Ivan. The back-to-back disasters slowed reconstruction, raised insurance costs and accelerated calls for stronger building codes and donor support.

title: Grenada Re-Establishes Diplomatic Relations with Beijing
description: In January 2005, with reconstruction financing needs surging after Hurricane Ivan, Grenada switched diplomatic recognition back from Taipei to the People's Republic of China. The change brought Chinese grants for the new national stadium and other infrastructure but ended Taiwanese aid programmes that had run since 1997.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission Final Report Published
description: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission released its final report in 2006, documenting human rights abuses across the 1970s and 1980s and recommending memorialization, education reform and continued search for the remains of Maurice Bishop and other victims of the 1983 events. The report has shaped subsequent debate on commemoration but did not produce prosecutions.

title: Tillman Thomas and the NDC Win Power
description: On July 8, 2008, Tillman Thomas led the National Democratic Congress to a 11-4 seat victory over Keith Mitchell's NNP, ending 13 years of continuous NNP rule. The Thomas government inherited a deteriorating fiscal position, the global financial crisis fallout and continuing reconstruction obligations from the 2004 and 2005 hurricanes.

title: Global Financial Crisis Triggers Grenadian Recession
description: The global financial crisis hit Grenada hard through collapsing tourism receipts, foreign direct investment and remittances, producing a contraction in real GDP and rising unemployment. The downturn deepened public debt distress and forced the Thomas government to negotiate emergency support from the IMF and World Bank.

title: Bernard Coard and Last Grenada 17 Prisoners Released
description: In September 2009 to early 2010, Bernard Coard and the remaining members of the Grenada 17 were released from Richmond Hill Prison after sentence reductions and a successful Privy Council ruling on resentencing. Their release closed a quarter-century of incarceration and reopened public debate on accountability for the 1983 killings.

title: Mitchell Returns to Power in NNP Landslide
description: On February 19, 2013, Keith Mitchell led the New National Party to a second 15-0 sweep of the House of Representatives, defeating Tillman Thomas's NDC amid economic distress and dissatisfaction with austerity. The result returned Mitchell to office for a fourth term and concentrated all parliamentary representation in a single party.

title: Government Defaults on Sovereign Debt and Seeks Restructuring
description: In March 2013, days after taking office, the new Mitchell government suspended payment on US dollar bonds and EC dollar securities, formally entering sovereign default and seeking a restructuring of around US$262 million in commercial debt. The default reflected unsustainable post-hurricane borrowing and triggered a multi-year IMF-supported adjustment programme.

title: IMF Extended Credit Facility and Fiscal Responsibility Law
description: In June 2014 the IMF approved a three-year Extended Credit Facility for Grenada and the government enacted a Fiscal Responsibility Law setting binding rules on the primary balance, public debt and wage bill. The framework underpinned the most ambitious fiscal consolidation in the country's history and reset expectations for budgetary discipline.

title: Citizenship-by-Investment Programme Reinstated
description: Grenada's parliament reinstated the Citizenship-by-Investment programme in 2013-2014, offering passports in exchange for real estate investment or contributions to a National Transformation Fund. CBI revenues rapidly grew to become a major budget line, financing infrastructure, debt servicing and post-default fiscal recovery.

title: Voters Reject Constitutional Reform Referendums
description: On November 24, 2015, Grenadians voted on seven constitutional amendment bills covering issues including replacement of the Privy Council with the Caribbean Court of Justice as final court of appeal, term limits for the prime minister and a fixed election date. All seven were defeated, with the CCJ proposal rejected by roughly 56% of voters.

title: Second Constitutional Reform Referendum Also Defeated
description: On November 6, 2017, voters rejected two further constitutional amendment proposals: the establishment of a Rights and Freedoms charter and a renewed proposal to adopt the Caribbean Court of Justice. Lower turnout and continuing public scepticism about the political class doomed Grenada's second attempt at constitutional reform within two years.

title: Mitchell NNP Wins Third 15-0 Sweep
description: On March 13, 2018, the New National Party again won all 15 parliamentary seats under Keith Mitchell, the third such clean sweep in Grenada's history. The result reflected economic stabilization under the IMF programme and a fragmented opposition but again left parliament without an elected opposition presence.

title: Grenada Completes IMF Extended Credit Facility Programme
description: In May 2017 (final review concluded 2018) Grenada successfully completed its three-year IMF Extended Credit Facility, restoring access to international capital markets after the 2013 default. Public debt fell from over 100% of GDP to under 70% and the primary balance moved into substantial surplus, making Grenada an IMF reform showcase in the eastern Caribbean.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Triggers Tourism Collapse and State of Emergency
description: Grenada confirmed its first COVID-19 case in March 2020 and imposed a state of emergency, curfews, border closures and a halt to commercial flights that crushed the tourism-dependent economy. Real GDP contracted by an estimated 13.8% in 2020, the steepest single-year decline since modern records began, and CBI revenues partly cushioned the fiscal blow.

title: Dickon Mitchell Leads NDC to Surprise Victory
description: On June 23, 2022, the National Democratic Congress under 44-year-old lawyer Dickon Mitchell, no relation to Keith Mitchell, won 9 of 15 seats and defeated the New National Party after nine years in office. The generational change ended the elder Mitchell's parliamentary career and brought a new cohort of Grenadian leaders to government.

title: Government Reviews Citizenship-by-Investment Governance
description: The new Dickon Mitchell government announced reviews of the Citizenship-by-Investment programme, project approvals and use of National Transformation Fund proceeds amid US and EU pressure on Caribbean CBI schemes. Reforms to due diligence, fee floors and transparency followed regional coordination among OECS CBI states.

title: Hurricane Beryl Devastates Carriacou and Petite Martinique
description: On July 1, 2024, Hurricane Beryl made landfall on Carriacou as a Category 4 storm, the earliest Atlantic Category 4 on record, destroying or damaging an estimated 98% of buildings on Carriacou and Petite Martinique. Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell described the dependencies as effectively flattened and called for emergency international assistance and renewed global climate action.

title: Government Declares National Disaster and Launches Reconstruction Plan
description: Following Hurricane Beryl, the Dickon Mitchell government declared a state of emergency on Carriacou and Petite Martinique, mobilized regional CDEMA assistance and launched a reconstruction programme financed by CBI proceeds, multilateral lenders and bilateral grants. The disaster reinforced the case for climate-resilient building codes and parametric insurance instruments.

title: Continued Implementation of Beryl Reconstruction and Climate Resilience Agenda
description: Through 2025 the Dickon Mitchell government continued implementation of the Hurricane Beryl reconstruction plan for Carriacou and Petite Martinique alongside resilience investments funded by the World Bank, Caribbean Development Bank and CBI receipts. Grenada also continued its diplomatic push at COP and IMF/World Bank meetings for concessional climate finance for small island states.

title: Grenada Wins Its First-Ever Olympic Medal: Kirani James's 400m Gold
description: On August 6, 2012, sprinter Kirani James won the men's 400m gold medal at the London Olympics in a national-record time of 43.94 seconds, becoming the first non-American to break 44 seconds in the event. The win gave Grenada, a nation of roughly 110,000 people, its first-ever Olympic medal of any color. James's victory made him a national hero and put Grenada on the global sporting map.
